children: is seeing longer delivery times for its latest premium iPhones, with JPMorgan pointing to firmer demand for the Pro models in the early preorder period, according to a Sunday research note.
JPMorgan said average wait times for the iPhone 18 Pro reached 23 days in the second preorder week, up from seven days previously. The Pro Max increased to 30 days from 19 days.

The U.S. and Germany recorded notable increases, while delivery periods in China remained below year-earlier levels. The U.S. represents about 34% of iPhone shipments, compared with roughly 19% for China, making the two markets important indicators of demand.
Longer lead times can reflect stronger customer interest, although supply limitations can also affect delivery schedules. JPMorgan said timelines could moderate during the third preorder week.

Other research has pointed to continued interest in the higher-priced models. Morgan Stanley said two-to-four-week waits despite increased production may indicate healthier demand, while an Evercore ISI survey showed 53% of prospective U.S. buyers planned to choose an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, up from 51% previously.
Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone and later production revisions could provide additional clues on demand trends.

title: JPMorgan Delivers Bullish Message For Apple Stock Fans
